page_title: Open Versus Closed: A Cautionary Tale

sources.entry: Open Versus Closed: A Cautionary Tale - Shows that open and closed load models disagree on response time and scheduling gains, with rules for choosing one.

summary.title: Open Versus Closed: A Cautionary Tale
summary.one_liner: Open and closed load-generation models can give different response-time and scheduling results, so the choice of model must match the real workload.
keywords: how to choose load model for testing
takeaways: Open systems (requests arrive independently) and closed systems (fixed users wait for responses) can produce different response-time results for the same system.
Scheduling policy gains measured under a closed model may not hold under an open model, and the reverse can also happen.
The paper gives rules for picking an open or closed model based on how the real workload behaves.
Using the wrong load model in testing or simulation can lead to misleading performance conclusions.
summary.summary: This NSDI 2006 paper by Schroeder, Wierman, and Harchol-Balter compares open and closed system models for load generation and evaluation. It shows that the two models can disagree on mean response time and on how much a scheduling policy helps. The authors give guidance on which model to use for a given setting. The page itself is only a citation and BibTeX entry; the full analysis is in the linked paper, which this summary does not describe in detail.
